---
title: "Posterior-draw scale validation and performance"
---

phit's posterior-draw kernels are timed against equivalent R matrix calculations, after their complete outputs are compared. The [raw report](draws-results.json) keeps every timing sample, comparison error, input hash, batch count, machine, runtime version, and thread setting.

## Methods

| Item | Setting |
| --- | --- |
| Workloads | Population and unbiased moments, covariance map, and affine draws at four draw and parameter sizes |
| Data | Python `random.Random(20261012)`, saved as JSON shared by PHP and R |
| Machine | AMD Ryzen 9 9955HX virtual machine, 2 cores, 7.8 GiB, Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS (x86_64) |
| Software | Rust 1.99.1, PHP 8.5.12 (phit 0.4.3 release build, no BLAS), R 4.6.2 (BLAS `libblas.so.3.12.0`), jsonlite 2.0.0 |
| Threads | OpenBLAS, OpenMP, MKL, and BLIS thread variables set to 1 |
| Repetitions | One warm-up, then five measurements; calls are batched (see [timing boundaries](#reproduction-and-timing-boundaries)) |
| Statistic | Median milliseconds per call |
| Timed | Complete result arrays, including PHP input conversion, validation, and allocation |
| Excluded | Startup, input generation, JSON parsing and serialization, and reference comparison |
| Memory | Not measured |

## Numerical agreement first

The run compared weighted means, both covariance normalizations,
covariance maps and log determinants, and **every transformed draw value** against
R. All quantities passed $10^{-11}+10^{-11}|\mathrm{reference}|$.

| Draws | Parameters | Values compared | Maximum absolute difference |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1,000 | 4 | 4,058 | 5.11e-15 |
| 4,000 | 16 | 64,802 | 3.91e-14 |
| 10,000 | 32 | 323,138 | 5.33e-14 |
| 100,000 | 8 | 800,210 | 2.11e-14 |

R uses normalized weights, `colSums`, `crossprod` of square-root-weighted centered
draws, `chol`/`backsolve`, matrix multiplication and `determinant(logarithm=TRUE)`.
The independent [80-digit fixtures and identity tests](../draw-numerics.qmd#independent-verification)
separately constrain covariance-map orientation, affine round trips and determinant
sign/scale. Benchmark verification compares PHP/R results; ordinary tests provide
the algebraic identity and edge-case checks.

## Recorded timings

Median milliseconds per call, including complete output materialization:

| Draws | Parameters | API | Population moments | Unbiased moments | Covariance map | Affine draws |
| ---: | ---: | :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1,000 | 4 | R | 0.052 | 0.054 | 0.016 | 0.035 |
| 1,000 | 4 | PHP | 0.1289 | 0.1299 | 0.001578 | 0.1909 |
| 4,000 | 16 | R | 0.69 | 0.66 | 0.022 | 0.49 |
| 4,000 | 16 | PHP | 2.048 | 2.046 | 0.01755 | 2.363 |
| 10,000 | 32 | R | 4.7 | 4.5 | 0.038 | 4 |
| 10,000 | 32 | PHP | 11.94 | 11.93 | 0.06364 | 10.97 |
| 100,000 | 8 | R | 9.1 | 7.3 | 0.019 | 6.5 |
| 100,000 | 8 | PHP | 26.68 | 26.72 | 0.00522 | 36.21 |

PHP's moments/affine calls include conversion from nested PHP numeric arrays to
owned Rust vectors, strict validation, numerical computation and conversion back
to PHP arrays. R starts from already numeric matrices and does not implement all
of PHP's validation/rank policies. This is an API-level workload comparison, not
a measurement of isolated matrix multiplication. Map timings depend only on
parameter count; the corresponding draw count labels the surrounding workload.
Compensated sums in Rust and R's BLAS cross-products have different arithmetic
and runtime costs.

## Reproduction and timing boundaries

Build using the [matching PHP/header environment](../development.qmd), then run:

```sh
cargo build -p phit --release --locked
# R and jsonlite are benchmark-only development dependencies.
PHP=/opt/homebrew/bin/php python3 tests/benchmarks/run-draws.py
# Optional overrides: RSCRIPT, STATS_EXTENSION; --repeats 5 --output /path/report.json
```

Python 3's standard library generates inputs with `random.Random(20261012)`.
Draws have a shared Gaussian component, independent Gaussian noise and parameter
means increasing by 0.1. Nonuniform weights have deterministic zeros every 11th
row. Covariances are constructed from deterministic full-rank lower factors.
The affine matrix includes off-diagonal mixing and a reflection, with a nonzero
shift. Temporary JSON inputs are identical for PHP and R; their SHA-256 hashes
are retained in the report. No intercept column is added.

Each worker loads JSON once. Startup, input generation, JSON parsing/serialization
and reference comparison are outside timed calls. Input loading is recorded
separately. Both APIs compute complete result arrays/matrices in each timed call;
PHP includes native input conversion, validation and result allocation. Timings
also include ordinary runtime reclamation of prior results.

R's elapsed timer has millisecond resolution. Each map measurement batches 1,000
calls. Moments/affine batch 1,000 calls for the 1,000 × 4 case, 100 for 4,000 × 16,
and 10 for both larger cases; the reported value divides by the batch count.
This avoids zero small-call readings but still limits R timing precision. R's
garbage collection and machine load contribute variation; raw measurements are
available for review. This run does not measure peak memory, Linux, PHP-FPM,
Stan evaluation, PSIS or complete moment-matching iterations.
